evidence: A screen on the food study's basis and mix rules, recombined: each blend is one case built from the three mixes' rules, with heat, dimming, N2O and methane from the totals. The weights come from a stated rule over a 5% grid. The heritage meat uses Earth's global per-kilogram land use and FAO GLEAM's methane intensities for a basket of the author's examples. No crop, livestock, grassland, climate or ecosystem model runs here.
reading_rule: As the food study: areas km2, power and heat TW, phosphorus Mt a year, N2O kt N and ppb, methane Mt a year and ppm at steady state, pairs [low-cost end, high-cost end]. weights are shares of the diet. blend[population][land rule] is the chosen blend; reference_planned_case and per_tenth_planned_case are at 8 billion under the compromise. light_taken_km2 is the fields' area plus the area-equivalent of the added dimming under fusion. heritage_meat cases are named population_level and give Mt of meat a year, its land, its share of the homestead region and of the diet's animal protein [20%, 25% protein], and the cattle's methane per kg of fat- and bone-free meat [retail, boneless carcass yield], with steady ppm at the soil sink's fast and slow ends.

criterion.rule: least light_taken_km2 at the high-cost end of the planned case, then summed over both ends, then least heat; light_taken_km2 is the fields' area plus the added dimming under the supply as a share of the Moon's surface

assumptions.basket_note: The author's examples: homestead dairy and vaca vieja (beef from dairy herds), some wagyu (beef from beef herds), heritage pork and chicken. The shares are a design guess.
assumptions.heritage_in_the_diet: The heritage meat stands within the diet's animal part, which the blend makes as microbial protein; share_of_animal_part gives its protein against that part, so the blend's power is left as computed.

sources: Poore, J. & Nemecek, T. 2018. Reducing food's environmental impacts through producers and consumers. Science 360, 987-992; per-kg land use as given by Our World in Data (ourworldindata.org/grapher/land-use-per-kg-poore).
Gerber, P.J. et al. 2013. Tackling climate change through livestock. FAO, Rome.
Opio, C. et al. 2013. Greenhouse gas emissions from ruminant supply chains: a global life cycle assessment. FAO, Rome.
IPCC 2006. Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories, volume 4, chapter 10 (enteric fermentation, Tier 1).
USDA ERS 1992. Weights, Measures, and Conversion Factors for Agricultural Commodities and Their Products. Agricultural Handbook 697, Table 7.
